info.title: Ever Platform API: instance-facing contract
info.description: The calls an installation of an Ever product makes to Ever Platform: the operations that accept an instance token, the public operations a product calls (key manifest, connect, statistics, lookup salt) and the two Ever ID reads a product makes with the token of a person who signed in. Every operation carries `x-ever-row`, its row in the outbound-call table. Errors are `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`.

post.summary:
Redeems a connect code with the installation's own Ed25519 connect key (Flow A): creates the
instance (or reconnects this organization's disconnected instance holding the same key) and
pins the key. A 24-hour code (`ever_sh`, `provisioning`, `partner`) redeems as
`pending_approval`: until an owner or admin approves it, every instance route but
`GET /v1/instances/me` answers `403 instance_pending_approval`. Unknown, expired, revoked,
consumed and malformed codes answer one byte-identical `422 code_invalid`; ten wrong codes in
an hour from one caller answer `429`. A replay with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the
original answer.

parameters.description:
Client-generated key, unique per principal, at most 128 characters; remembered 24 h.
The same key with the same request replays the first answer (`Idempotency-Replayed:
true`); with a different request it answers `422 idempotency_mismatch`.

post.summary: Product receipt for a deletion or export request
post.description:
Each connected product removes its own `(issuer, subject)` rows and
applies its own account policy to the accounts Ever controls, then
answers honestly (`deleted`, `anonymised`, `retained_legal`,
`no_account`, `failed`, or `exported` with a signed URL of its own
export). For an account held by another controller (a self-hosted or
partner instance, an Ever Cloud tenant with other members) it removes
only its link rows, notifies that controller and answers
`forwarded_to_controller` with `detail.controller_kind` and
`detail.notified_at`. Unacknowledged requests are flagged to
support after 7 days; the job continues. Idempotent by `(job_id,
instance)`.

get.summary:
The calling installation's effective states: its installation-wide integrations, and per live
tenant link its per-link ones. A self-hosted installation reads every integration off until an
owner or admin of the linked organization enables it; nothing is written by this read.
Installations re-read it when `ever.consent.integration.*` reaches their feed.

heartbeat that omits it lifts the deny. An installation may never switch an integration on
(`422`); with `reason: instance`, `404` when no state exists (the SDK treats it as already
off).

post.summary:
Rotates the instance's connect key: the new key signs assertions from now on, the replaced key
keeps minting tokens for 7 days (`previous_valid_until`), and tokens already minted stay valid
until they expire. The body proves the rotation twice: `current_key_proof` is signed with the
current connect key (the key it replaced is not accepted, even during the overlap) and
`new_key_proof` with the new key; both carry the claims of a client assertion with
`aud = <api origin>/v1/instances/me/keys` and `cnf.jkt` = the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the new
key, and each `jti` is used once. Only one replaced key is kept: rotating again inside the
overlap (proved with the then current key) drops the older key at once, with every token minted
with it (the way to cut a compromised key now). The new key must be an Ed25519 public JWK no
installation holds or held; the platform assigns its `kid`.

parameters.description:
Client-generated key, unique per principal, at most 128 characters; remembered 24 h.
The same key with the same request replays the first answer (`Idempotency-Replayed:
true`); with a different request it answers `422 idempotency_mismatch`.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

Links the installation's anonymous statistics id to it (integration `stats_link`, enabled by
the organization that connected it after the operator's local accept; never on an installation
Ever operates). The statement is signed with the statistics key, names the installation (`sub`:
its instance id) and the call is authenticated with the connect key, so only an installation

ConnectKind.description: The kind of deployment an installation is.

Options chosen on the consent screen. No integration takes any: only an empty object (or
none) is accepted, anything else answers `422`. A consent record is immutable, so nothing
free-form ever enters it.

dpa_version.description: The data-processing agreement version shown (must be the current one).

scope_version.description: The scope version shown on the consent screen (must be the current one).

ConsentUrl.description: The consent deep link a product opens.

url.description:
The link into app.ever.co (`/connect/consent?...`); the person must be an owner or admin
of the linked organization.

Context.description: The authoritative view of who the caller is and what they may act on.

identities.description: Every active identity of the person (hints only).

orgs.description: The organizations the identity acts for.

orgs_filtered.description: The organizations withheld, with the reason and the step-up.

tenants.description: The person's tenants (for the platform's own clients).

ContextFiltered.description: One organization withheld from the identity.

oneOf.description: The step-up that would reach it.

enterprise_org_id.description: For an enterprise identity: its organization.

ContextLink.description: One tenant link of an organization.

ContextOrg.description: One organization the identity acts for.

enforce_for_members.description: Whether it enforces company sign-in for members.

Currency.description: ISO 4217 code for money, or a platform unit code such as `XEC` (credits) listed by `GET /v1/currencies`.

Delivery.description:
One delivery series of an event to an endpoint. `error` is a category (`timeout`, `dns`,
`tls`, `http_<status>`, `ssrf_blocked`), never the receiver's body.

attempt.description: The attempt number of the series.

error.description: The category of the last failure.

id.description: The delivery id (`X-Ever-Delivery`; a new id for each attempt series).

next_attempt_at.description: When the next attempt is due.

response_status.description: The receiver's status of the last attempt.

items.description: The deliveries of this page, newest first.

next_cursor.description: The cursor of the next page, `null` on the last.

DeviceRequest.description: Device-first connect; the instance shows the user code and polls for the token.

device_code.description: 32 random bytes, base64url; held by the instance only.

client_assertion.description: RFC 7523 assertion signed by the key presented at `POST /v1/connect/device`.

DiscoverableFeature.description: Additive vocabulary of what a discoverable organization advertises to counterparties.

EndpointOwner.description: The owner of an endpoint, as the API shows it.

EnvelopeActor.description: `{kind, id}` of who caused an event (never an e-mail or a name).

EnvelopeSubject.description: `{kind, id}` of the entity an event is about.

ErrorCode.description:
Every machine code the API answers with. Additive: new codes may appear; clients treat an
unknown code by its HTTP status.

EventEnvelope.description:
One event on a webhook, the installation feed or SSE. Payloads carry identifiers and status
only, never records; delivery is at-least-once: dedupe on `id`.

data.description: Typed per `type`; the schema is published in the catalog.

occurred_at.description: When the state change happened (UTC, milliseconds).

subject.description: The entity the event is about.

last_id.description: The cursor of the last event processed.

acknowledged.description: The acknowledged cursor (an older acknowledgement changes nothing).

FeedResponse.description: A page of the installation's events.

events.description: The events after the cursor, in feed order.

has_more.description: Whether more events wait after this page.

last_id.description:
The cursor of the last event returned (the request's own when none was): pass it as
`after` and to `ack`.

The newest position of this feed: re-read the state through REST, then acknowledge this
cursor and continue from it (`after`).

FeedResync.description: `410 resync_required`: the problem, with the cursor to continue from.

FieldError.description: One field-level failure of a validation problem.

message.description: A human sentence. Never personal data.

path.description:
A JSON pointer into the body (`/handle`), `?name` for a query parameter or `#Name` for a
header.

Handle.description:
Organization handle as shown at `ever.co/<handle>`. Lowercase ASCII,
letter first, 3-30 characters, single hyphens only, no leading, trailing
or double hyphen. Handles belong to organizations only.

notices.description: Compact hints; the feed carries the full events.

recorded.description: Whether this heartbeat was recorded (one a minute is).

integrations_denied.description:
The integrations its operator denies for every organization
(`EVER_CONNECT_INTEGRATIONS_DENY`; `*` denies every one). Sent, it replaces the stored list:
a denied integration reads `denied_by_policy` and switches off; one no longer listed may be
enabled again by an organization. Absent, the stored list is kept.

module_version.description: The version of its Ever Connect module.

version.description: The product version (`major.minor.patch`, optional short suffix).

Identifier.description: An organization's own identifier. The value is stored encrypted and never returned.

discoverable.description: Whether it is opted in to counterparty lookup.

IdentifierHashes.description: Salted identifier hashes pushed by a connected instance on behalf of a linked organization (integration `counterparty_discoverable`). Values never leave the instance.

IdentityHint.description: A linked identity, as a hint (the full subject is never listed).

org_id.description: For an enterprise identity: its organization.

subject_hint.description: The last four characters of the subject.

IdentityResolveRequest.description: For product backends that hold only an ID token. Returns the context shape; `orgs`, `orgs_filtered` and `links` are scoped to the calling instance (organizations with an active tenant_link on it; the caller filter).

id_token.description: When present it is verified and must match `issuer`/`subject`.

Install.description: The install fact, not the mechanics; `next_action_url` tells the caller where to continue (deep link, checkout, product admin).

state.description: Same vocabulary as `p_listings.install.state` and the event `install_state`: `cancelled` = stopped before it was installed (`requested | pending_payment | installing`), `removed` = removed after `installed | delivered`.

InstallSource.description: How the instance was installed; set only through the template's environment, never by fingerprinting.

InstallStatus.description: Reported by the instance that performed an `instance_plugin` install.

Instance.description:
A connected instance as an organization sees it. Instances are outbound-only: no address is
ever derived, and none is shown here.

connection_owner.description:
Whether the calling organization connected it (and so may change, approve or disconnect
it); absent on the instance's own view.

disconnected_at.description: When it was disconnected, while it is.

last_seen_bucket.description:
How recently it was seen: `now`, `lt_1h`, `lt_24h`, `lt_7d`, `lt_30d`, `gt_30d` or
`never`.

owner_org_id.description: The organization that connected it (the instance's own view only).

stats_linked.description: Whether a consented stats link exists (the stats id itself is never shown).

tenant_links.description: The calling organization's tenant links to it (one instance's read only).

version.description: The product version it last reported.

InstanceEntitlement.description: A signed entitlement document as an installation receives it.

document.description:
The compact JWS (`ever.entitlement.v1`, `typ` `ever-entitlement+jwt`); verify it with the
key set at `/.well-known/ever-keys.json` and store the bytes as received.

expires_at.description: When the document expires; the offline grace (`ever.grace_s`) follows.

InstanceIntegrationPut.description: An installation switches one integration off (it may never switch one on).

reason.description: `instance` (the operator switched it off) or `policy` (the operator's deny list).

tenant_link_id.description: The tenant link, for a per-link integration.

InstanceIntegrations.description:
The effective states of the calling installation: its installation-wide integrations, and
per tenant link its per-link ones.

catalog_version.description: The catalog version the states refer to.

links.description: Per tenant link id, its per-link integrations by key.

InstanceKey.description: The connect key an instance holds (its id and rotation; never the key itself).

InstanceSelf.description: What an instance sees about itself.

tenant_links.description: Its tenant links that are not unlinked.

IntegrationAccept.description: The operator's local accept or decline of an installation-wide integration waiting for it.

consent_id.description: The consent the state waits for.

IntegrationPut.description: Enable (with an explicit consent) or disable one integration on one installation.

tenant_link_id.description: The tenant link, for a per-link integration (absent for an installation-wide one).

IntegrationState.description:
The effective state of one integration on one installation (and tenant link), with its
consent's provenance.

config.description: Non-secret options chosen at consent time.

consent_id.description: The consent in force, when there is one.

dpa_version.description: The data-processing agreement version it was consented to.

granted_by_person_id.description:
Who granted it: your own id when it was you, else `null` (another member, a deleted
person, or the cloud terms).

operator_accept.description:
`pending`, `accepted` or `declined` for an installation-wide integration of an
installation a customer or a partner operates; `null` elsewhere.

scope_version.description: The scope version it was consented to.

tenant_link_id.description: The tenant link (`null` for an installation-wide integration).

updated_at.description: When the state last changed (`null` when there is no state yet).

IntegrationStateBrief.description: The effective state of one integration, briefly.

config.description: Non-secret options chosen at consent time.

consent_id.description: The consent in force, when there is one.

scope_version.description: The scope version it was consented to.

state.description:
`available` (off, can be enabled), `enabled`, `disabled`, `revoked`, `denied_by_policy`,
`pending_operator` (waiting for the installation operator's local accept) or `coming_soon`.

IntentComplete.description: Callback from the product after a consented hand-off completed its part of the provisioning intent. Idempotent by `jti`.

Jwk.description: Ed25519 public key in JWK form.

kid.description: Key id. For instance keys `kid = base64url(sha256(pub)[0:8])`.

KeyManifest.description:
`GET /.well-known/ever-keys.json`. A JWKS of Ed25519 keys wrapped in a
manifest signed by the long-lived root key that every SDK release pins.
Verifiers trust an `entitlement`, `assertion` or `intent` key only through
a valid manifest. Keys rotate every 90 days with a 30-day overlap.

manifest.description:
Compact JWS signed by a pinned root key. Header
`{"alg":"EdDSA","kid":"<root kid>","typ":"ever-key-manifest+jwt"}`;
payload `{"iss":"https://api.ever.co","iat":<unix s>,"exp":<iat + 30 d>,
"keys_sha256":"<hex sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical keys array>",
"root_kid":"<root kid>"}` (see the entitlement document format).
Validity is the payload's `iat`/`exp`; there are no separate
timestamps in the response.

keys.description: The keys the manifest vouches for.

manifest.description:
A compact JWS signed by a pinned root key; payload `{iss, iat, exp, keys_sha256,
root_kid}` where `keys_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical `keys` array.

KeyRotate.description:
A new connect key and the two proofs that authorize the rotation. Each proof is a compact JWS
with the claims of a client assertion (`iss = sub = <instance id>`, a random `jti` of 16-128
characters used once, `iat`, `exp` at most 300 s after `iat`) whose `aud` is
`<api origin>/v1/instances/me/keys` and whose `cnf.jkt` is the RFC 7638 thumbprint of
`public_jwk`. An instance token alone never rotates a key.

current_key_proof.description:
The proof signed with the installation's current connect key (the key it replaced is not
accepted, even during the overlap).

new_key_proof.description: The proof signed with the new key (the installation holds the key it installs).

public_jwk.description: The new Ed25519 public JWK (no installation may hold it yet, or have held it).

kid.description: The new key's id (sign assertions with it now).

previous_valid_until.description: Until when the replaced key still mints tokens.

Legal.description:
The legal texts every consent screen links: one data-processing agreement covers every
integration, and one public list names every sub-processor.

dpa_version.description: Its version, equal to every integration's `dpa_version`.

LinkedTenant.description: A tenant link as the instance sees it (never who linked it).

display_name.description: The product tenant's name as reported.

product_org_id.description: The product organization, when there is one.

product_tenant_id.description: The product tenant (`*`: the whole installation).

ListingCard.description: Public card projection produced by the type plugin.

LookupRequest.description: `hash = hex_lower(sha256(salt_bytes || ":" || kind || ":" || utf8(normalized)))`. Up to 100 hashes per query.

LookupResponse.description: Unknown hashes are absent (no negative list). `features` is the intersection of what the organization advertises and what it is entitled to.

ManagedOperationResult.description: What the instance reports for one operation. Status and size only; never file names, paths, URLs, log lines or backup content.

artefact_ref.description: Opaque reference of the backup in the customer's own storage.

ManifestKeyBody.description: One key of the published key set.

not_after.description: When a rotated-out key stops verifying (RFC 3339), `null` while active.

not_before.description: When the key began to sign (RFC 3339).

MembershipLink.description: One active tenant link of an organization.

MeterKey.description: The meter key set of the `ever.entitlement.v1` document. Credit balances are not meters; they are read from the ledger (`GET /v1/orgs/{org}/credits`).

MirrorBatch.description: Identifier-and-status mirror pushed by the source product's Ever Connect outbox. <= 500 ops, <= 4 MiB. Per-item idempotency by `(external_id, external_version)`.

external_version.description: Monotonic per external id; a lower or equal version is `ignored_stale`.

Money.description: Money is always integer minor units plus a currency; never decimals.

amount_minor.description: Amount in the currency's minor unit (cents for EUR/USD).

MyMembership.description: One authoritative membership of the caller (claims inside tokens are only a hint).

client_secret.description: Returned exactly once, on the first `ready` read.

OidcClientRequest.description: Ask the platform to create the OIDC client that lets this instance offer "Sign in with Ever ID" (integration `ever_id_login`).

logout_uri.description: Back-channel logout endpoint of the instance.

OrgProfilePush.description: Consented organization profile fields pushed by an instance (integration `profile_import`). Only the declared fields are accepted.

source_of_truth.description: When true the admin chose the product as the source for these fields and the organization's own fields are overwritten.

Page.description:
Cursor pagination envelope. Every list endpoint returns `items` and
`next_cursor` (`null` when the page is the last one). Order is
`(created_at DESC, id DESC)` unless the endpoint says otherwise. There are
no offsets and no totals.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor to pass as `?cursor=` for the next page.

PersonLinkCreate.description: Reported by a connected instance when a local user links an Ever ID. Identifiers only; never an e-mail.

display_name.description: Product tenant display name (not the person's name).

PricingModel.description: Pricing is delegated to the app; `external` means the vendor bills on its own site.

code.description: The machine code, stable for clients to branch on.

detail.description: The code followed by a human sentence. Never personal data or secrets.

instance.description: The request id (`x-request-id`); filled in by the API for every problem it sends.

retry_after_s.description:
Seconds until a retry can succeed (`rate_limited`, `idempotency_in_progress`); mirrors
`Retry-After`.

ProductCode.description: The Ever product a record belongs to. `demand` is listed with status `soon` and accepts no connections.

RedeemRequest.description:
Code-first connect: the installation redeems a connect code with its own Ed25519 connect
key, which becomes its credential. The connect key never signs anonymous statistics (those
have a key of their own). The body carries no address or any other field outside this
schema: an instance's public address is set by the organization in app.ever.co, or later by
the instance through a consented integration. The optional `return_origins` are not stored:
the platform keeps a digest of each, to refuse a consent link that would return anywhere
else.

install_source.description:
Where it was installed from, read from its environment (`self-hosted`, `ever.sh`,
`partner:<slug>`, ...); never inferred.

public_jwk.description: Its connect key: an Ed25519 public JWK (`kty: OKP`, `crv: Ed25519`, `x`).

return_origins.description:
The origins (`https://host[:port]`; plain `http` only on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or
`[::1]`) the installation's consent links may return to, at most four. Only a digest of
each is kept, never the address; a consent link naming another host is refused. Absent or
empty: the installation's consent links carry no return address. A reconnect replaces
them when it names any.

serves_products.description: The products it serves besides its own (a Gauzy API serving Teams).

oneOf.description: The tenant to link when the code pre-binds the organization.

RedeemResponse.description: The connected installation and where it calls next.

instance_id.description: The instance id: the assertion's `iss` and `sub`.

keys.description: The key manifest as `/.well-known/ever-keys.json` serves it.

kid.description: The key id the platform assigned to the presented key (the assertion's `kid`).

oneOf.description: The tenant link the redeem created (a code that pre-binds the organization).

status.description:
`active`, or `pending_approval` (an owner or admin approves it with the key's
fingerprint; until then every instance route but `GET /v1/instances/me` answers `403`).

token_endpoint.description: `POST` an assertion here for a token.

RedeemTenant.description: The tenant the redeem links when the code pre-binds the organization.

display_name.description: The product tenant's name, shown to the organization.

product_tenant_id.description:
The product tenant's id (a multi-tenant product; a single-organization product links the
whole installation).

SaltSet.description:
Active salt versions. The salt is public by design; privacy comes from
the one-way hash, opt-in only answers, feature-scoped results, rate
limits and the rule that queried hashes are never persisted or logged.
A new version is added with `active_from`; the old one answers until
`retire_after` (>= 180 days).

SecretRotated.description: A rotated secret: the new one, shown once, and how long the old one keeps signing beside it.

previous_valid_until.description: Until when deliveries also carry a signature made with the previous secret.

SemVer.description: Product version string as reported by the instance.

StatsAccepted.description: The answer to an accepted report.

superseded.description:
`true` when an earlier report of the same `instance_id` and `period` arrived the same UTC
day and was replaced (absent otherwise).

StatsLinkCreate.description:
`POST /v1/instances/me/stats-link`: the installation links its anonymous statistics id to
itself. The statement is signed with the statistics key and names this instance; the call is
authenticated with the connect key, so only an installation holding both can link them.

statement_sig.description:
A compact JWS (`alg: EdDSA`, `typ: ever-stats-link+jwt`) signed with the statistics key
over `{stats_instance_id, stats_public_jwk, sub, iat}`, where `sub` is this instance's id
(the subject of its instance token), at most ten minutes old.

stats_instance_id.description: The anonymous statistics id (UUID v4) the installation reports under.

stats_public_jwk.description: The statistics key (the one its reports are signed with).

StatsLinked.description: The answer to a link: nothing beyond the status (the statistics id is never returned).

StatsPublicJwk.description: The statistics key of a link request, as a JWK (`kty: OKP`, `crv: Ed25519`).

x.description: base64url (no padding) of the 32 public-key bytes.

StepUp.description: How to reach a withheld organization.

identity.description: The identity to sign in with: `personal` or `enterprise`.

TenantLink.description:
"ever.co/acme is the same organization in Gauzy, Teams, Works": one product tenant bound to
one organization on one instance.

display_name.description: The product tenant's name as reported at link time.

product_tenant_id.description: The product's tenant id; `*` when the instance is the organization.

state.description:
`active`, `suspended`, `orphaned` or `unlinked`. `orphaned`: the instance or the product
tenant vanished while the organization still exists; the product tenant keeps running.

TenantLinkCreate.description:
Redeem a link code: the product workspace becomes the same organization as the one that
minted the code.

display_name.description: The product tenant's name, shown to the organization.

TenantLinkRekey.description: Re-key an installation-wide tenant link to one product organization, once the product gained organizations (Ever Traduora - the `*` link becomes the id of the default organization).

TestVectors.description: Normalization and hash vectors every SDK must pass.

TokenRequest.description:
RFC 7523 client authentication with the `client_credentials` grant. The assertion is a
compact JWS (`alg: EdDSA`, `typ: JWT`, `kid`) signed with the connect key, with claims
`iss = sub = <instance id>`, `aud = <api origin>/v1/instances/token`, a random `jti` (16-128
characters, used once), `iat`, and `exp` at most 300 s after `iat`.

access_token.description: `evit_…`: opaque, one hour; keep it in memory only.

UsageReadings.description: Push alternative to the pull probe (integration `usage_reporting`).

app_deployment_id.description: Mirrored App deployment the reading belongs to (Ever Works hosting readings; units `cpu_hour`, `gb_month`, `request_k`).

UsageReport.description: Instance-reported meters (integration `usage_reporting`). Only meters listed in the consented configuration are accepted; anything else answers 422.

event_filter.description: 1 to 50 exact types or prefixes ending in `.*`, among the types this owner may receive.

url.description: `https://` on port 443 or 8443, at most 2048 characters, a public address.

secret.description:
The signing secret (`whsec_…`), shown once: `X-Ever-Signature-256: t=<unix>,v1=<hex
HMAC-SHA256(secret, t + "." + body)>`, verified within 5 minutes.

WebhookCreated.description: A registered endpoint with its signing secret, shown this once.

WebhookEndpoint.description:
A webhook endpoint. The signing secret is never shown after creation; `secret_prefix` tells
secrets apart.

api_version.description: The `data` version delivered for types that dual-emit.

event_filter.description: Exact event types or prefixes such as `ever.registry.*`.

last_success_at.description: The last delivery the receiver accepted.

secret_prefix.description: The first characters of the current signing secret.

status.description: `active`, `paused` (by its owner) or `failed` (after consecutive dead deliveries).

url.description: Where events are posted (HTTPS; private address ranges are refused).

status.description: `paused` stops deliveries; `active` resumes them and resets `failure_streak`.

url.description: A new URL (same rules as at registration).
